Keeps the microphone on while a notification is visible, and reacts when you say “Hello École Eyes”. Android may stop it to save battery. Turn it off at any time.

ÉCOLE EYES is designed so that you stay in control.

Microphone: the microphone is used only after you tap the voice button, or while hands-free listening is on (a notification is always visible). Speech recognition is performed by the speech service installed on your phone, which may send audio to its provider unless on-device recognition is selected. ÉCOLE EYES does not record or store audio.

Camera: photos are taken only when you ask. When cloud AI is allowed, a reduced-size photo is sent once to the AI service to describe it, then discarded. It is never saved by the app.

Documents: the app can read only folders and files you explicitly allow, and you can remove access at any time. Document text is sent to the AI service only when you ask for a summary or explanation.

Conversation: your conversation history is stored encrypted on this phone. You can clear it by voice (“clear my history”) or from Settings.

Backend: the AI key is kept on a server you control; it is never inside this app.

Safety: camera descriptions can be wrong or incomplete. ÉCOLE EYES is not a safety device and cannot guarantee that a path is free of obstacles. Keep using your cane, guide dog or other trusted aids.

Contacts, calls, location and notifications: used only when you ask. A call is placed only after you say yes; emergency numbers only open the dialer. Your location is put into a text message that you send yourself. Contacts, location and notifications are never sent to the AI service or stored. Notes you dictate are stored encrypted on the phone until you delete them.
Welcome to École Eyes. Tap the big button in the middle of the screen and speak. Say “what can you do” to hear what I can help with.
Hello! I am École Eyes. How can I help you?

I can describe what is in front of you, read text on signs and paper, tell colours, find and read your documents, answer questions, take notes, set reminders, call your contacts, read notifications and help in an emergency. Many of these work without internet. Just speak naturally. Say stop at any time to silence me.
The volume is already at maximum.
The volume is already at minimum.
I have nothing to repeat yet.
Camera open. Say “describe what is in front of me” or “read the text”.
Documents. Say “find a document named…” or “read my latest PDF”.
File search. Say the name of the file you want.
You are already on the home screen.
Your conversation history has been cleared.
Hands-free listening is on. Say Hello École Eyes when you need me.
Sorry, I did not understand. You can say “what can you do”.

Before we start, a few important things. To understand questions, describe photos and explain documents, I send your request, and only when you ask, a reduced photo or document text, to a secure AI service. Nothing is saved there by this app. You can change this in settings. Do you agree? Say yes or no.
Thank you. Cloud assistance is on.
Understood. Cloud assistance stays off. I can still read documents and text with the phone alone.
Cloud assistance is turned off. Say “allow cloud assistance” or open settings to turn it on.
There is no internet connection. I can still read documents and text with the phone alone.

I can describe what the camera sees, but I can make mistakes and I cannot guarantee that the way ahead is safe. Please keep using your cane or guide.
Continuous description is on. I will tell you when something changes. Say stop to end it.

Say “Hello École Eyes”. Tap to open the app.
Emergency screen. You can say: call my emergency contact, call emergency services, or share my location.
Emergency mode. Stay calm, I am here. If you are in immediate danger, say: call emergency services.
Do you want me to call %1$s now? Say yes or no.
You have not chosen an emergency contact yet. Do you want me to open the dialer with the emergency number %1$s? Say yes or no.
Other options: say call emergency services, share my location, or set a name as my emergency contact.
I could not start the call on this phone.
The dialer is open with %1$s. The call button is at the bottom centre of the screen; double tap it to call.
I did not find a contact named %1$s.
To find people by name, I need permission to read your contacts. They are only read on this phone.
Without access to contacts I cannot find people by name. You can say a phone number instead.
To call directly, I need permission to make phone calls. I always ask you before calling.
Without that permission I will open the dialer and you press call yourself.
To share your location, I need permission to use it. It is read only now, and put in a message that you send yourself.
Without location permission I cannot share where you are.
Finding your location. This can take a few seconds.
I could not get your location. Try again near a window or outside.
Do you want to send your location to %1$s by text message? Say yes or no.
The message with your location is ready for %1$s. The send button is usually at the bottom right; double tap it to send.
Your position is latitude %1$s, longitude %2$s. Choose an emergency contact in settings so I can prepare a message for them.
I need help. My location: %1$s (sent with ÉCOLE EYES)

Tell me when, for example: remind me in 10 minutes to take my medicine.
To show reminders when they are due, I need permission to post notifications.

To read your notifications, turn on notification access for ÉCOLE EYES in the screen I am opening, then come back. Notifications stay on your phone.

I cannot read the battery level on this phone.

Without internet I can still read your documents and printed text in Latin letters, roughly describe objects, people and colours, tell the time and date, take notes, set reminders, make calls and read notifications.
Detailed scene descriptions, conversation, summaries, Arabic or handwritten text and banknotes need the internet.
You are online and cloud assistance is on, so all features are available.
Cloud assistance is off, so everything stays on this phone.
No AI server is set up, so I work on this phone only.
Recognizing banknotes needs the internet and cloud assistance; doing it on the phone alone would not be reliable enough.
The on-device analysis did not work this time. Please try again.
If you are in danger, call emergency services first. If it is safe, stay where you are, speak loudly to people nearby, and keep the phone in your hand.
